prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1110; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the claimant's vehicle on the driver side rear quarter panel. Claimant reports neck pain and headache at the scene and was transported by ambulance for evaluation. Police report requested.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant reports being diagnosed with a concussion and is experiencing dizziness, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and states they are handling the claim directly. Explained the claims process and requested copies of all medical records and discharge paperwork.

Entry 3: Received the police report. Responding officer noted both vehicles were in adjacent lanes, the insured was merging left, and contact occurred at the rear of the claimant's vehicle. Insured statement obtained and consistent with the report. Photos of both vehicles received and added to file.

Entry 4: Claimant provided initial medical documentation confirming concussion diagnosis and a recommendation for follow-up with a neurologist and a period of restricted activity. Reviewed the documentation and noted the claimant's symptoms have been reported consistently across the medical notes. Advised claimant that a separate bodily injury evaluation will follow once treatment is complete.

Entry 5: Claimant called to ask about the status of the vehicle damage estimate and whether a rental vehicle is available. Confirmed the estimate is under review and that rental coverage is being verified under the policy. Reminded claimant to keep all treatment appointments and to send any new bills or records as they arrive. Diary set for follow-up in two weeks.
